workflow: Direct dataset patch; no cards gate claimed. Independent semantic review pending.

claims.claim: Proto-porcelain became more widespread during the Zhou dynasty.
Zhou dynasty 1027–221 BCE as bounded period of increased prevalence; not an onset date.
dated_assertion records broader prevalence without asserting a specific recipient or route.
China is broad scope of abstract, not a particular distribution site.

sources.original: Yin, M. (2012), UCL doctoral thesis abstract, https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/1380281/
sources.reading: Existing source record and saved abstract excerpt; rechecked live UCL repository abstract 2026-11-10. Full thesis was not evaluated.

duplicate_screen.search: Case-insensitive proto-porcelain/proto porcelain across data/discoveries and data/leads.jsonl; only target discovery matched.

control.subject: initial appearance of proto-porcelain in China
control.decision: Already represented by /events/0; do not add a second Shang event.

proposed.subject: increased prevalence of proto-porcelain
proposed.scope: China, broad period; receiving sites and route unspecified
proposed.decision: Distinct later development extends existing record; description already mentions it, but no corresponding event existed in snapshot.

questions: Can original archaeological site reports independently clarify locations, chronology and meaning of wider prevalence?
Would a later schema explicitly representing spread better capture a general change in prevalence without implying a named receiving community?
limitations: An abstract-level assertion; not a site-by-site demonstration or a new independent corroborating source.
This is a proposal, not an independent review; existing research basis is not upgraded.
A separate source record preserves the existing shared source file while citing the same author and abstract; it is not independent evidence.
